overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 23
overview.text: In this lesson, you will investigate standard HSA.REI.C.5 in depth: proving why adding a multiple of one equation to another creates a new system with the exact same solution set. This property provides rigorous justification for the elimination method.
outcomes: Understand that adding a multiple of one equation to another produces a new equation satisfied by the same coordinates.
Prove that replacing an equation with a linear combination generates an equivalent system of equations.
Strategically choose multipliers to eliminate a variable and solve 2×2 linear systems.
overview.teacherInsight: Demonstrate that if $A = B$ and $C = D$, then $A + kC = B + kD$. Because the point $(x,y)$ makes both statements true, it must make any combination of them true as well.

content.html:
The Mathematical Theorem of Linear Combinations

Theorem (HSA.REI.C.5):

Given a system of two equations $\begin{cases} E_1 = 0 \\ E_2 = 0 \end{cases}$, any new system formed by $\begin{cases} E_1 = 0 \\ cE_1 + dE_2 = 0 \end{cases}$ (with $d \neq 0$) has the exact same solution set as the original system.

vocabulary.definition: An algebraic technique where equations are added or subtracted to cancel out one of the variables.
An expression constructed from a set of terms by multiplying each term by a constant and adding the results.
Two systems of equations that have the exact same solution set.

practiceQuestions.question: Solve the system using elimination: $\begin{cases} 2x + 3y = 12 \\ 5x - 3y = 9 \end{cases}$
practiceQuestions.explanation: Add both equations to eliminate $y$: $(2x + 5x) + (3y - 3y) = 12 + 9 \implies 7x = 21 \implies x = 3$. Substitute into first equation: $2(3) + 3y = 12 \implies 6 + 3y = 12 \implies 3y = 6 \implies y = 2$. Solution is $(3, 2)$.

practiceQuestions.question: Why does multiplying an equation by a non-zero constant $k$ NOT change its solution set?
options: Because multiplication is reversible by multiplying by $\frac{1}{k}$, preserving the exact truth value.
Because multiplying by a constant changes the graph into a circle.
Because constants cancel out automatically in algebra.
It actually does change the solution set.
practiceQuestions.explanation: By the Multiplication Property of Equality, $A = B \iff kA = kB$ for any non-zero real number $k$. The step is completely reversible.
